To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the in-plane electric field in Cu+Au collisions is strong and comparable to the out-of-plane magnetic field; (2) the in-plane electrical field can strongly suppress the charge-dependent two particle correlation γ q 1q 2, and even reverse its sign; and (3) the in-plane and out-of-plane fields are not correlated with each other, which means that the charge separation in the out-of-plane direction is not induced by the in-plane electric-field.

in Cu + Au collision at 200 GeVAu + Au collisions, the electric field can be strong, and it is in-plane, and it can last long enough for its effect to be seen in the charge-dependent two particle correlator γq1q2.
the in-plane magnetic fields in non-central heavy ion collisions can be very strong and the in-plane electric field can be as strong as the magnetic field in the early stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electromagnetic fields and the chiral magnetic effects in Cu + Au collision.
the study of the chiral anomaly and chiral magnetic effects in heavy-ion collisions.
the general properties of electromagnetic fields in non-central heavy-ion collisions and their impacts on γ q 1q 2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CME is still not excluded in Cu+Au collisions, but that the results of the STAR Collaboration are not sufficient to claim its existence in this system.
the CME is not the dominant source of γ q 1q 2 in the 0-30% central Au+Au collisions at RHIC.

the chiral magnetic wave (CMW), a collective mode of chiral anomaly, is the most likely origin of the charge-dependent two-hadron correlators observed in the RHIC Beam Energy Scan (BES) and the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chiral magnetic wave and elliptic-flow driven mechanism are not compatible with each other.
the CME signal can be enhanced by choosing the appropriate collision system and event centrality.
we should be careful when we use γ q 1q 2 as a tool for detecting CME in non-central heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in-plane magnetic field in Cu + Au collision is too weak to drive the CME and γ q 1 1 q 1 2 is mainly induced by the elliptic flow.
the in-plane electromagnetic fields in heavy-ion collisions should be taken into account when interpreting the experimental measurements.
the in-plane electromagnetic fields are very important and should be taken into consideration in the studies of the CME in heavy ion collisions.
